steps.title: Where to start: what "supplement" means
steps.body: The key word is "supplement". Two angles are supplementary when they add up to $180^\circ$, a straight angle. So the supplement of an angle is whatever is missing to make a straight line.

your_turn.prompt: As a warm-up, what is the supplement of $120^\circ$?

steps.title: Set up an equation
steps.body:
Call the unknown supplement $x$. Together with $85^\circ$ it must make $180^\circ$. Careful: the complement would use $90^\circ$ instead; here it is $180^\circ$.
$$x + 85 = 180$$

your_turn.prompt: Is $85^\circ$ acute or obtuse? So will its supplement be acute or obtuse?
your_turn.answer: $85^\circ$ is acute (less than $90^\circ$), so its supplement is more than $90^\circ$, which is obtuse.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: Subtract $85$ from both sides: $x = 180 - 85 = 95$. Check: $85 + 95 = 180$. The answer is **$95^\circ$**.
